# Tucson all-time extremes
**All-time Tucson daily and monthly extremes** **for the period (1894-2026)** **Temperature****Record High:**117 deg F on June 26, 1990 **Record Low:**6 deg F on January 7, 1913 **Warmest year (avg.):**73.3 deg F in 2017 **Warmest month (avg.):**94.2 deg F in July 2023 **Coolest year (avg.):**65.0 deg F in 1905 & 1912 **Coldest month (avg.):**41.2 deg F in January 1937 **Precipitation****Record one-day (mid-mid):**3.93 inches on July 29, 1958 **Wettest year:**24.17 inches in 1905 **Wettest month:**8.06 inches in July 2021 **Driest year:**4.17 inches in 2020 **Driest month:**0.00 inches in December 2024 (last of 107 occurrences) **Snowfall****Record one-day (mid-mid)**6.8 inches on December 8, 1971 **Record yearly total:**8.3 inches in 1987 **Record seasonal (July-June)**6.8 inches in 1971-72 season Check NOWdata for additional historical climate data for Tucson & other sites across SE Arizona

This is a list of the largest annual precipitation totals ever recorded in Tucson, Arizona history from 1894–2026.
What Was the Wettest Year in Tucson History?
According to NOAA records, the most precipitation that Tucson, Arizona has ever received in a single calendar year is 24.2 inches which occurred in 1905.
Year to date though November 7, 2026: 10.9 inches
